b1_facts: a is congruent to b (mod n) means that n divides a - b; equivalently, a and b leave the same remainder when divided by n.
b2_facts: a is congruent to b (mod n) means that n divides a - b; equivalently, a and b leave the same remainder when divided by n.
If a is congruent to b (mod n) and c is congruent to d (mod n), then a + c is congruent to b + d (mod n).
If a is congruent to b (mod n) and c is congruent to d (mod n), then a x c is congruent to b x d (mod n).

b1_facts: Fermat's Little Theorem: if p is prime and a is not divisible by p, then a^(p-1) is congruent to 1 (mod p).
b2_facts: Fermat's Little Theorem: if p is prime and a is not divisible by p, then a^(p-1) is congruent to 1 (mod p).
Exponent reduction: if a^k is congruent to 1 (mod n), then a^m is congruent to a^(m mod k) (mod n).
If a is congruent to b (mod n), then a^k is congruent to b^k (mod n) for any positive integer k.
The remainders of the successive powers a^1, a^2, a^3, ... (mod n) eventually repeat in a cycle.

b1_facts: A number is divisible by 3 if and only if its digit sum is divisible by 3.
b2_facts: A number is divisible by 3 if and only if its digit sum is divisible by 3.
A number is divisible by 9 if and only if its digit sum is divisible by 9.
A number is divisible by 11 if and only if the alternating sum of its digits is divisible by 11.
A number is divisible by 4 if and only if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.
A number is divisible by 6 if and only if it is divisible by both 2 and 3.

b1_facts: Euclidean algorithm: gcd(a,b) = gcd(b, a mod b).
b2_facts: Euclidean algorithm: gcd(a,b) = gcd(b, a mod b).
For positive integers a and b, gcd(a,b) x lcm(a,b) = a x b.
In terms of prime factorizations, the gcd of two numbers takes the minimum exponent of each prime, and the lcm takes the maximum exponent of each prime.

b1_facts: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic: every integer greater than 1 factors uniquely into primes.
b2_facts: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic: every integer greater than 1 factors uniquely into primes.
Divisor-count formula: if n = p1^a1 * p2^a2 * ... * pk^ak, then n has (a1+1)(a2+1)...(ak+1) positive divisors.
1 is not a prime number, and 2 is the only even prime number.

b1_facts: To convert a number to base b, repeatedly divide by b and read the remainders in reverse order.
b2_facts: To convert a number to base b, repeatedly divide by b and read the remainders in reverse order.
Positional value: a digit d at position i (counting from 0, rightmost) contributes d * b^i to the value.
